key_insight: LongMemEval-V2 provides a targeted benchmark that measures whether agent memory systems truly internalize environment-specific experience (affordances, dynamics, workflows, failure modes) rather than merely storing short user traces or optimizing downstream task scores.
problem_solved: Existing memory benchmarks focus on user histories, short traces, or end-task success and do not directly evaluate whether agents have learned and retained actionable, environment-specific experience needed for long-term competence in specialized web environments.
method: Design a benchmark suite (LME-V2) of simulated specialized web environments and tasks that require recalling interface affordances, state dynamics, recurring workflows, and failure modes over long horizons.
Provide probing tasks and metrics that directly test memory retention and use (e.g., affordance recall, workflow re-use, failure-mode recognition) rather than only task completion.
Supply an evaluation protocol and baseline agent integrations so researchers can measure how different memory architectures and update strategies affect long-term experiential learning.
impact: LME-V2 gives practitioners a focused tool to diagnose and improve long-term memory components of agents, enabling more robust, efficient, and adaptive behavior in real-world web and workflow automation settings.

paper_title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
paper_authors: Di Wu, Zixiang Ji, Asmi Kawatkar, Bryan Kwan, Jia-Chen Gu
